_comment: tools/vtable-policy.json -- WHY A SLOT THIS TREE CAN TYPE IS STILL NOT
EXPOSED, one entry per method, in prose.
THIS IS NOT VERIFICATION AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ANY. The engine factory
interfaces are stable: the version string is the contract, and it changes
when the layout does. What is written here is POLICY -- a judgement about
what managed code may be allowed to do -- and policy is not a fact about
WHERE IT SHOWS UP. tools/vtable-layout accepts a slot it cannot type on an
exposed interface only with a reason here (or a C++ proxy), so an untypeable
slot always has an account of itself. A slot it can type may carry a reason
too: what a refusal decides is that no managed binding reaches that method.
THE GENERATOR REQUIRES EVERY KEY TO NAME A REAL DECLARATION in the class
it is filed under, so a method renamed in a header takes its reason with
it rather than leaving a comment on nothing.
These 72 reasons were written against five interfaces over several lanes
and are carried verbatim from the C# ledgers that used to hold them.

SetSeed: returns nothing, so its only observable is its effect, and on this
engine build seeding through it does not reseed the stream the other
three draw from. Refused a second time on the rule that managed code
may ask for server randomness and may not be a source of it.

GetModelFrameCount: its answer has exactly one other source in this process and that
source is the ABI path -- SourceSharp_ModelFrameCount, compiled from
the same header this slot number was read out of. Two derivations that
share a header agree with each other and are wrong together the moment
the shipped engine differs, which is the failure the whole instrument
exists to catch. Nothing else in the process knows how many frames a
model has: the count lives on the loaded model and there is no second
door into it. Bound the day one appears, and not before.

Read: slot 0, so its only neighbour is Write. A control that writes through
a file handle to prove an index is not one worth running, and no other
Write: not read-only; nothing on this boundary needs it.
Open: neighbours are Write and Close, and Close takes a FileHandle_t --
handing it the filename deletes a CFileHandle that is a string. No
adjacent slot is callable and the handle it returns is not a value
Close: returns void, so its only observable is its effect. Refused on the
Seek: takes a FileHandle_t, which only the refused Open can produce.
Tell: takes a FileHandle_t, which only the refused Open can produce.
Flush: takes a FileHandle_t, which only the refused Open can produce.
Precache: loads a file into a cache. A control with a side effect is not a
IsFileWritable: as FileExists, and nothing on this boundary calls it.
ReadFile: takes CUtlBuffer &, which is a C++ object this side cannot construct.

ClientCmd_Unrestricted: slot 106 and 26 compiled call sites, the heaviest method on this
interface that is not varargs -- and it RUNS A CONSOLE COMMAND. It
returns void, so its only observable is its effect, which is
IUniformRandomStream::SetSeed's ground; and the effect changes the
game, which is LoadModel's. Slot 105 dereferences a Vector & and slot
107 sets a restriction flag, so there is no control beside it that
could be run either. A wrong index here would execute an arbitrary
string as a console command. ONE MEMBER uses it, by integrator ruling
throws for anything but `connect ...` and runs only what SecureLaunch
passed through stock's safe-character check. Unrestricted because the
client state restricts commands from construction and connect is not
FCVAR_CLIENTCMD_CAN_EXECUTE, so stock sent it this way too.
ExecuteClientCmd: slot 102 and 16 call sites. It runs a console command too, so it is
ClientCmd: slot 7 and 17 call sites. Not a member: it is reached through members
named for their purpose (Reconnect, RequestManagedReload, JoinTeam,
SpectatorCommand, SubmitConsoleLine), since managed code may run console commands (user,
2026-10-05, plan_client_novalve.md 8). The raw slot adds nothing they need.
IsPlayingDemo: slot 76 and 20 call sites. It answers one bit, the bit is false
whenever this gate could ask, and a wrong slot returning zero AGREES
with it -- so the comparison could not fail. GetLocalPlayer's ground
(asserting a constant) and FileExists' (a control that agrees) at
GetAchievementMgr: slot 114 and 13 call sites. It returns a pointer to an IAchievementMgr
and nothing else in this process knows what that pointer should be;
there is no second door into it. GetModelFrameCount's ground.
IsHLTV: slot 86 and 14 call sites. One bit, false on every map this gate runs,
and its neighbour IsPlayingTimeDemo answers the same bit.
GetPlayerInfo: slot 8 and 12 call sites -- below the floor all along. It WRITES a
player_info_t through a pointer and the process has no second
statement of what belongs in one.
GetAppID: slot 104 and 2 compiled call sites, and it WOULD HAVE PASSED -- which
is why it is written down. Measured live under this gate it answers
243750, which is exactly what steam.inf in the mod directory says
(`appID=243750`) and what the SDK base's steam_appid.txt says, both
read by System.IO with no engine in the route. Refused anyway, because
that agreement is a property of the ENVIRONMENT and not of the index:
the engine asks the STEAM CLIENT for the app id and falls back to a
hard-coded 215 when there is none -- a freshly dlopen'd engine with no
Steam answers 215, measured. A row that passes when Steam happens to be running and fails
when it is not is not holding a slot against a second source; it is
reporting the weather. Its 243750 is kept as corroboration of the
Con_NPrintf: varargs, and a varargs call cannot be issued through a fixed indirect
signature at all -- whatever the transport. The heaviest single method
on this interface at 44 compiled call sites, and it needs a native
entry point. Slot 29, so the floor never covered it and nothing about
it changed. THE FIXED-ARITY THUNK WAS COSTED AND NOT BUILT, which is
written down so it is not re-proposed as though it were free. It would
work and it would be safe: `engine->Con_NPrintf( pos, "%s", text )` in
C++ passes the text as an ARGUMENT and never as the format string, and
the slot is the COMPILER'S rather than one this side derived, so no
managed index is in it. shell_standalone_player.cpp:201 already does
exactly that, so the pattern is in the tree. What stops it is the
price: a thunk is a 468th EngineApi slot, taking the ABI from 603
fields to 604 and its version from 217 to 218 -- and `no C++ was added
and no ABI slot was added` is the headline result this whole binding
exists to hold. It is a transport decision for a lane that can move
those numbers, not something a refactor may do on the way past.
GetMaxClients: slot 21, and gpGlobals->maxClients would be a genuine second source: a
struct field from globalvars_base.h read through a raw pointer, with
no vtable index anywhere in it. Refused because it has ZERO compiled
IVEngineClient), which is the ground docs/plan-audit.md §3.12 drops
IDataCache and ISceneFileCache on. Surface with no demand behind it.
GetLevelVersion: slot 52, and it has the STRONGEST available proof of anything on this
interface -- gpGlobals->mapversion, and the map revision at byte 8 +
64*16 of the .bsp, which System.IO can read without the engine at all.
Refused anyway, on the same ground as GetMaxClients: zero compiled
call sites. Recorded because a bar that only ever excludes the
unprovable is not a bar; this one excludes something provable.
GetDXSupportLevel: slot 47 and 15 compiled call sites, so the demand is real and the slot
is below the floor. Its answer has one other source in this process --
the mat_dxlevel convar -- and managed code has no way to read a convar
it did not declare, so there is nothing to hold it against. Bindable
the day there is; not before.
IsInGame: slot 26, and its neighbour IsConnected (27) answers the same bit
whenever the assertion could be made. A control that AGREES is not a
control -- IBaseFileSystem::FileExists' ground exactly -- and picking
a further slot that happens to disagree would be picking a control to
IsConnected: as IsInGame, and the two are each other's problem.
Time: slot 14. gpGlobals->curtime is the only other clock in the process and
the client's is not the server's; asserting they are close is a
tolerance, and this file has no tolerances.
GetLocalPlayer: slot 12. On a listen server the answer is 1, and asserting a constant
is not holding a slot against a second source.
GetScreenSize: slot 5. The only other statement of the window size in this process is
the -w/-h the harness itself passed, so the row would be checking the
test against the test -- and a window the engine legitimately sized
differently would read as a wrong index.
LoadModel: slot 13 and 25 compiled call sites. It LOADS a model that is not
loaded, so the method under test has a side effect on the engine's
model cache, and each of its control slots would have that side effect
GetViewAngles: slot 19 and 29 compiled call sites, the heaviest below the floor. It
writes through a QAngle & and the process has no second statement of
where the local player is looking.
SetViewAngles: slot 20; not read-only, and nothing on this boundary needs it.
IsPaused: slot 84 and 8 call sites, the heaviest thing left in the band. One
bit, false whenever this gate could ask, and its neighbour
IsTakingScreenshot (85) answers the same bit. IsPlayingDemo's ground
IsTakingScreenshot: slot 85 and 4 call sites, and IsPlayingTimeDemo slot 78 with 4. As
IsPaused: one bit each, false under the gate, and each has a neighbour
GetScreenAspectRatio: slot 95 and 6 call sites. The only other statement of the window's
shape in this process is the -w/-h the harness itself passed, so the
row would be checking the test against the test. GetScreenSize's
ground exactly, and it was below the floor all along.
DebugDrawPhysCollide: slot 73 and 8 call sites. It DRAWS, and it takes a CPhysCollide *, an
IMaterial * and a matrix3x4_t & that this side cannot construct. A
side effect and no callable shape.
ComputeLighting: slot 67 and 5 call sites. It writes a Vector & and an array of them,
and the process has no second statement of what the light at a point
SaveAllocMemory: slot 70 and 4 call sites, with SaveFreeMemory (71). They allocate and
free engine memory; the observable is the effect. SetSeed's ground.
GetNetChannelInfo: slot 72 and 3 call sites. It returns an INetChannelInfo * and nothing
else in this process knows what that pointer should be.
MapHasHDRLighting: slot 103 and 1 call site, and this one was MEASURED before it was
refused. Its second source is real and independent: LUMP_LIGHTING_HDR
is lump 53 of the .bsp and System.IO reads its length at byte 8 +
53*16 with no engine in the route -- the same shape of route that
binds IVEngineServer::GetMapEntitiesString. On dm_lockdown, the map
every gate here runs, that lump is ZERO BYTES, so the engine answers
false and a wrong slot returning zero AGREES with it. IsPlayingDemo's
ground, arrived at by reading the map rather than by arguing. Bindable
on a map whose HDR lump is not empty -- and choosing such a map to
make the row pass would be choosing a control to make a row pass.
GetMapEntitiesString: slot 93, and it is PROVABLE and PROVED -- by the identical measurement
LUMP_ENTITIES of the loaded .bsp, byte for byte, read by System.IO
with no engine and no index in the route. Refused on GetMaxClients'
ground: ZERO compiled call sites in this client, against ONE in the
server. The third thing this bar excludes that could have passed, and
the first where the same method binds on the other side of the
IsLowViolence: slot 117 and 2 call sites, with GetUILanguage (91). Both answer a
property of the ENVIRONMENT -- a Steam setting, a -language on the
command line -- so a row would pass or fail on how the machine is
configured rather than on the index. GetAppID's ground.
GetPausedExpireTime: slot 134 and 2 call sites. Unpaused it answers a constant, and
asserting a constant is not holding a slot against a second source.
GetMouseDelta: slot 127 and 2 call sites, and it is one of the two declarations the
whole floor problem is about. It writes two int & and the process has
no second statement of how far the mouse moved.
SetGamestatsData: slot 125 and 2 call sites, with ServerCmdKeyValues (128) and
SetAchievementMgr (113). Setters and senders. Not read-only, and the

IsWindowedMode: slot 139 and 1 call site. Its only other source is the -windowed the
harness itself passed -- GetScreenSize's ground -- and it is already
GetProtocolVersion's +1 control, which is the job it is good for.

Time: slot 49 and 12 compiled call sites, the second heaviest. The shipped
slot answers a wall clock and gpGlobals->curtime is the only other
clock in the process; asserting the two are close is a tolerance, and
this file has no tolerances. IVEngineClient::Time's ground.
ServerCommand: slot 36 and 5 call sites. It queues a console command, returns void,
and its only observable is what that did -- SetSeed's ground and
LoadModel's at once, which is exactly why ClientCmd_Unrestricted is
refused on the client. A wrong index here would run an arbitrary
CreateEdict: slot 21 and 5 call sites. It ALLOCATES an edict out of the engine's
free list. The method under test changes the server's entity table,
and so would every control beside it.
PrecacheModel: slot 4 and 4 call sites, with PrecacheSentenceFile (5), PrecacheDecal
(6) and PrecacheGeneric (7). They precache -- the model is added to
the very string table IsModelPrecached is held against, so calling one
would move the second source. IBaseFileSystem::Precache's ground. Slot
7 is also the reason IsModelPrecached has no control BELOW it: it
takes a filename in the same first register, so an index one too low
would not fault, it would LOAD A FILE. SetFileWritable's ground
EmitAmbientSound: slot 27 and 3 call sites. It plays a sound to every client in the PVS.
A side effect with a network packet in it.
ClientCommand: slot 38 and 4 call sites. Varargs, which cannot be issued through a
fixed indirect signature at all -- and it runs a command on a client,
so it would be refused twice over.
Con_NPrintf: slot 46, and Con_NXPrintf slot 47. Varargs. The floor was never their
problem and nothing about them has changed.
Con_NXPrintf: slot 47. Varargs, exactly as Con_NPrintf at 46 -- and it is filed
here in its own right because the older ledger named it only inside
Con_NPrintf's prose, where a table keyed by method name could not
see it. A reason that lives inside another method's sentence is a
GetClientConVarValue: slot 55 and 3 call sites. Its answer is a convar's value on a
connected client, and managed code has no way to read a convar it did
the day there is one; not before.
IsDecalPrecached: slot 9, and IsGenericPrecached slot 10. Both are IsModelPrecached's
controls and both are in principle bindable the same way -- against
the "decalprecache" and "genericprecache" string tables. Neither has a
compiled call site worth the surface (1 and 0), and the negative half
of the law they would need is what makes them useful as controls.
Recorded so the next lane knows the route exists rather than re-
PvAllocEntPrivateData: SaveFreeMemory (26). They allocate and free engine memory; the
observable is the effect. SetSeed's ground.
LightStyle: A SETTER, and this impl is a read-only window on IVEngineServer.
beside it on the same ground.
